newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMPORT PRESSURE BEARS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR DOWN.
newsitem.headline: IMPORT PRESSURE BEARS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR DOWN.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed Monday's interbank session weaker on the U.S. unit, sterling and the mark largely due to an influx of importer demand for foreign currency which overwhelmed available export resources.
"It was initially a quiet market then due to a lot of demand we saw some panic (buying) in the market," one dealer commented.

"The central bank was nowhere to be seen but if there's still a shortage (of foreign currency) tomorrow morning they might come in," the dealer added, saying the Reserve Bank were likely to intervene if the local unit tested the 11.4050/4150 level on the key U.S. dollar.

The Zimbabwe dollar finished the day at 11.4000/4100 against the U.S. unit and was also quoted softer against sterling at 19.0810/1095 compared to Friday's 19.0240/0500 and at 6.3510/3575 from 6.3240/3300 versus the mark.
It however saw a slight gain on the rand at 2.4920/4940 from 2.4940/5000.
